cf.title: Gather rescan keeps the first scan's tuple bound in workers

input.subject: bug: Gather rescan keeps the first scan's tuple bound in workers

verdict_reasoning: The bug is a confirmed wrong-results bug with a default-settings repro in message #1, and the fix follows what ExecInitParallelPlan() already does. The only surviving objection is standards-compat-1: the patch says Backpatch-through: 14 and changes an exported function signature in back branches. That is a fixable choice, and message #2 already names the alternative. No level fails.

brief.title: Fix stale tuple bound in parallel workers on Gather rescan
brief.problem: When a Limit with a parameter-dependent count sits over Gather or Gather Merge and the node is rescanned, workers keep the tuple bound from the first scan. If a later scan needs more rows, the query silently returns too few rows, or with Gather Merge over a Sort the right number of wrong rows. The report says all supported branches are affected, back to Postgres 11.
brief.proposed_design: ExecParallelReinitialize() gets a tuples_needed argument and writes it into the shared executor state in the DSM segment, as ExecInitParallelPlan() already does. Gather and Gather Merge pass their current bound on rescan. A second, optional patch adds a regression test with the leader out of the scan.
user_visible_surface: C API: ExecParallelReinitialize() gains a tuples_needed argument, which changes an exported function signature in back branches.
author_claims: The bug is a wrong-results bug in all supported branches, introduced by commit 3452dc5240d in Postgres 11.
A bound that shrinks, or an unbounded first scan, is harmless and only loses the early exit.
The reporter's repro fails at default settings; with parallel_leader_participation = off the result is stable.
The patch author can reproduce it on master with a 1000-row table.
The patch author knows of no extension that calls ExecParallelReinitialize().
brief.thread_state: Jeff Davis reported the bug and confirmed it, and shihao zhong replied with a fix and a test. Nobody has reviewed the patch, and the back-branch ABI question is open.
unclear: The thread does not decide whether back branches keep the old ExecParallelReinitialize() signature and add a new function instead.
The material does not say whether other per-scan state in the DSM segment also goes stale on rescan.
The thread does not say whether the regression test is stable across platforms and runs.

objections.title: Back-branch fix changes the signature of an exported executor function
objections.failure_scenario: An extension built against an earlier 14-18 minor release calls ExecParallelReinitialize() with the old argument list. After a minor upgrade the server reads an undefined tuples_needed value. The workers then stop at a random bound, or the extension fails to build, and the user finds out only after the upgrade.
objections.argument: Patch 0001 says "Backpatch-through: 14" and adds a parameter to a function declared in execParallel.h. Minor releases normally keep exported signatures stable, so an extension does not need a rebuild. In message #2 the author says no caller is known and offers a new function as the alternative, but the thread does not choose. An absence of known callers is weak evidence for out-of-tree code that uses parallel contexts.
objections.author_must_show: Will the back-branch versions keep the existing ExecParallelReinitialize() signature, for example by setting the bound through a separate function, and leave the new argument only on master?

critic.reasoning: The commit message says "Backpatch-through: 14" and the patch changes a prototype in execParallel.h. Message #2 names the ABI-compatible alternative but the thread does not choose it, so the question is open and fixable.

refuted.title: Back-branch fix changes the signature of an exported executor function
refuted.failure_scenario: An extension built against 14.x-18.x calls ExecParallelReinitialize() with the old argument list. After a minor update it is not rebuilt, so the server reads an undefined value as tuples_needed, and workers may stop at a random bound. The result is wrong query results with no error.
refuted.argument: The 0001 commit message has Backpatch-through: 14 and changes the prototype in execParallel.h. Message #2 says the author knows of no caller but would add a new function if a committer prefers. The thread has not chosen between the two, and back-branch practice is to keep exported signatures stable. A committer would likely ask for an ABI-compatible variant for the back branches and a signature change on master only.
refuted.author_must_show: Will back branches keep the old ExecParallelReinitialize() as a wrapper or add a new function, with the signature change applied only on master?

refuted.title: Back-branch signature change of ExecParallelReinitialize() is left undecided
refuted.failure_scenario: An extension built against an older 14 to 18 minor release calls ExecParallelReinitialize() with the old argument list. After a minor upgrade, the server reads an undefined value as tuples_needed and writes it into the DSM segment. The workers then apply a random bound, which can again give wrong results, and nothing reports the mismatch.
refuted.argument: The patch carries Backpatch-through: 14 and changes an exported executor function in every branch. Message #2 relies on the author knowing of no callers, and that is not evidence about out-of-tree code. Message #2 also names the usual alternative, a new function or keeping the old signature as a wrapper, but the series does not choose it. A committer would likely ask for that choice before pushing to back branches.
refuted.author_must_show: Will the back-branch versions keep the old ExecParallelReinitialize() signature, for example as a wrapper or through a separate setter, and change the signature only on master?

refuted.title: Per-scan DSM fields still have two write paths that can drift
refuted.failure_scenario: A future patch adds a per-scan field to FixedParallelExecutorState and sets it only in ExecInitParallelPlan(). Rescans then reuse the old value, as tuples_needed did here. Users see wrong results years later under LATERAL or nested-loop plans, and no assertion or test catches it.
refuted.argument: Message #1 shows that this bug came from exactly that drift: 3452dc5240d updated the setup path but not the reinitialize path added earlier. The fix copies the assignment into a second place, so the two paths can still drift for the next field. The brief also notes that nobody has checked whether other shared per-scan state goes stale on rescan. One helper called from both paths, at least on master, would make the invariant harder to miss.
refuted.author_must_show: Have the other fields of FixedParallelExecutorState been checked for staleness on rescan, and could both paths share one function that sets the per-scan fields?

critic.reasoning: The scenario needs a future patch to add a per-scan field, so it is not a failure of this fix. The struct's other fields are param_exec, which ExecParallelReinitialize() already rewrites, and eflags and jit_flags, which do not change between scans.

doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Will the back-branch versions keep the existing ExecParallelReinitialize() signature, for example with a separate function that sets the bound, and change the signature only on master?
Is the 0002 regression test stable across platforms and repeated runs, given that it depends on which rows the workers read with the leader out of the scan?
Does the fix also cover the plain Gather case from message #1, and does the test exercise it or only Gather Merge?

committability.owner_note: Jeff Davis reported and confirmed the bug in message #1 but has not reviewed the patch. The owner needs to know the parallel executor's DSM reuse on rescan.
committability.liability: A back-patched executor change in all supported branches, including the ABI choice for ExecParallelReinitialize() and any buildfarm instability from the new test.
committability.author_follow_up: The patch author offered in message #2 to switch to a new function for back branches if the signature change is a concern.

priority.reason: The query returns wrong results without an error at default settings in all supported branches, and the fix is about 4 KiB in three executor files and one header. The plan shape needs a parameter-dependent Limit over a rescanned Gather or Gather Merge, so not every user hits it.

provisional_note: Without the code, this review could not check that both Gather and Gather Merge pass the current bound at the right point on rescan. It also could not check whether the test output is deterministic.

precedents_retrieved.title: Don't shut down Gather[Merge] early under Limit.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Don't shut down Gather[Merge] early under Limit.
Reverted commit(s): Fix buffer usage stats for parallel nodes.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Revert part of commit 19df1702f5.

Early shutdown was added by that commit so that we could collect
statistics from workers, but unfortunately, it interacted badly with
rescans.  The problem is that we ended up destroying the parallel context
which is required for rescans.  This leads to rescans of a Limit node over
a Gather node to produce unpredictable results as it tries to access
destroyed parallel context.  By reverting the early shutdown code, we
might lose statistics in some cases of Limit over Gather [Merge], but that
will require further study to fix.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix the statistics gathering in case of commit and chain
precedents_retrieved.summary: After `commit and chain`, the backend stays in a transaction, so `postgres.c` never calls `pgstat_report_stat()` and table statistics (and so autovacuum triggers) are not updated until a plain commit. The patch calls `pgstat_report_stat()` from the `if (s->chain)` branches in `CommitTransactionCommand()` in xact.c.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund worried that calling `pgstat_report_stat()` where it could not be called before is unsafe, for example if relations stay open across chained transactions, and he objected to the copied blocks. Tom Lane wanted the call in `CommitTransaction`, which needs a redesign of the `force` argument and of the idle timer handling; the two did not agree on that design. The author said she had no time to address Tom's review in that commitfest, and the visible messages show no revised patch.
matched_queries: Gather Merge wrong results LATERAL limit
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I'm a bit worried about triggering pgstat_report_stat() in new places where it
previously couldn't be called.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow setting parallel_workers on partitioned tables
precedents_retrieved.summary: Allow the parallel_workers reloption on partitioned tables, so that the planner uses it to choose the number of workers for a Parallel Append over the partitions. A later version also let grouping relations take the setting from the partitioned table they read, for partitionwise aggregation.
precedents_retrieved.objection: David Rowley questioned the semantics: a high setting on the partitioned table can request more workers than the partitions use, and the number does not shrink when the planner or run-time pruning removes partitions. Laurenz Albe and Amit Langote agreed the design needed more thought, and Amit Langote suggested a separate parallel_append_workers option. The thread then stalled, the patch stopped applying, and Daniel Gustafsson marked it Returned with Feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
If someone sets the partitioned table's parallel_workers high so that
they get a large number of workers when no partitions are pruned
during planning, do they really want the same number of workers in
queries where a large number of partitions are pruned?

precedents_retrieved.title: speeding up GIN build with parallel workers
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch splits a GIN index build between parallel workers, each scanning a range of heap blocks and building its own rbtree of entries. The workers send sorted entries through shared memory to the leader, which merges them and writes each key once; the leader later also takes part as a worker.
precedents_retrieved.objection: In April Robert Haas moved it to the next CommitFest because it had too little review and too few comments. He also found no parallel-safety check for expression indexes, workers opening the heap and index with no lock, and no agreement on the gin_shared_mem GUCs. Michael Paquier returned it with feedback mainly because of Heikki Linnakangas's suggestion to keep the rbtree but flush it to tapes and merge them with the tuplesort.c machinery from Peter Geoghegan's parallel B-tree patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: If we flushed the tree to a tape instead, then we could perhaps use the machinery that Peter's parallel B-tree patch is adding to tuplesort.c, to merge the tapes.

precedents_retrieved.title: Parallelize correlated subqueries that execute within each worker
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets the planner build parallel plans for queries with correlated subplans when each subplan runs entirely within one parallel worker, so no Param value has to pass between workers. After review, the design changed to treat PARAM_EXEC params as parallel safe by default, track required params on each rel, and insert a Gather node only where that set is empty.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The thread shows no author reply after Tomas Vondra's July 2024 review, and the entry was returned with feedback in October 2024. That review found that regression tests failed on a changed plan in select_parallel, reported a compiler warning, and listed code comments. It also said no reviewer was able to confirm that the PARAM handling is correct.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: And in general the patch looks reasonably simple and clean, but my knowledge of PARAM intricacies is pretty much nil, so I'm hesitant to claim the patch is correct.

precedents_retrieved.title: system load consideration hook for parallel workers
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Peter Eisentraut, Tom Lane, Peter Geoghegan
precedents_retrieved.summary: Before starting parallel workers, check the current system load and reduce the number of workers when the system is busy, so parallel query does not slow down other sessions at peak load. The author proposed a hook for this and later posted a POC patch that measures CPU load and picks the worker count from the free CPUs.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut argued that a load-based control for parallel workers alone is premature before there is field experience with parallel query, and that the problem covers all process types. He also did not trust system load metrics as a gatekeeper, since load averages lag by about a minute, and found the POC code platform-specific and poorly documented. He suggested refining the existing process-count settings instead, and closed the entry as not favored by the community.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
We don't yet have enough field experience with the parallel query
facilities to know what kind of use patterns there are and what systems
for load management we need.  So I think building a highly specific
system like this seems premature.

precedents_retrieved.title: Disable parallel query by default
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Tom Lane, Greg Sabino Mullane, Álvaro Herrera
precedents_retrieved.summary: Change the default of max_parallel_workers_per_gather to 0 so the planner does not pick parallel plans unless users turn parallelism on. The author reported that busy OLTP systems overload when frequent short queries flip to parallel plans and start many worker processes.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers held that if parallel plans are chosen too often, the fix is better cost estimation or tuning parallel_setup_cost, not turning the feature off. The closing decision was to keep the default: affected users can already set max_parallel_workers_per_gather to 0, and most users benefit from it being nonzero. Álvaro Herrera proposed better observability of parallel worker costs as follow-up work.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: This appears to have been the decision we took on this: we won't change the default; users affected by this can already turn max_parallel_workers_per_gather to 0; most users benefit from it being nonzero.

precedents_retrieved.title: Lock updated tuples in tuple_update() and tuple_delete()
precedents_retrieved.summary: When tuple_update() or tuple_delete() finds a concurrently updated tuple in read committed mode, the table AM locks the updated version itself instead of returning TM_Updated for a separate tuple_lock() call. Later versions also had update and delete return the old tuple through a slot passed by the executor, which avoids refetching it and helps table AMs with costly TID lookups.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Version 15 was committed in March 2023, then reverted after Andres Freund's post-commit review. He showed that RETURNING could use the wrong tuple, with an isolation test that fails. He also criticised the new API: the ignored wait parameter, tmfd turned into an input, and the LazyTupleTableSlot code. The redesigned old-tuple API came days before the version 16 feature freeze, and he said it was not ready for 16. In March 2024 the author planned to push a revised version, and the visible messages do not show why the entry was finally returned with feedback in October 2024.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I guess this really is part of my issue with this change - it optimizes the rare case, while not addressing the same inefficiency in the common case.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert exporting of internal GUC variable "data_directory".
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert exporting of internal GUC variable "data_directory".
Reverted commit(s): Use GUC lexer for recovery.conf parsing.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This undoes a poorly-thought-out choice in commit 970a18687f9b3058, namely
to export guc.c's internal variable data_directory.  The authoritative
variable so far as C code is concerned is DataDir; there is no reason for
anything except specific bits of GUC code to look at the GUC variable.

After yesterday's commits fixing the fsync-on-restart patch, the only
remaining misuse of data_directory was in AlterSystemSetConfigFile(),
which would be much better off just using a relative path anyhow: it's
less code and it doesn't break if the DBA moves the data directory of a
running system, which is a case we've taken some pains over in the past.

This is mostly cosmetic, so no need for a back-patch (and I'd be hesitant
to remove a global variable in stable branches anyway).

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found that tried this fix or rejected it for a reason that applies here. [P1] reverted an early Gather shutdown that broke rescans, and [P4] restored a rescan test; neither recorded reason applies to restoring the tuple bound on rescan, and [P20] has no recorded reason.
Apart from the back-branch ABI point, the fix adds no syntax, GUC, catalog or dump change, and users see only corrected query results.

The fix adds no on-disk, WAL, catalog or wire-protocol state. The bound lives only in the per-query DSM segment, which is created and freed with the query, so the only issue for this angle is back-branch ABI.

The fix has no privilege or exposure aspect. It rewrites one field in the shared executor state that only the leader writes and only its own workers read, during a rescan the user already triggers. It adds no new SQL surface, setting, role or way to see other sessions' data, and gives an unprivileged user no new way to use resources. The wrong results come from the existing bug, not from the fix, and a stale bound that is too large only loses the early exit.

The fix itself is not in doubt: it is a confirmed wrong-results bug, the change adds no cost for non-parallel or non-rescan plans, and it fits core. The objections above concern how the fix is backpatched and how drift is prevented.

This is a wrong-results bug fix in the executor's Gather rescan path, and no existing feature, setting or extension can give workers the current tuple bound after a rescan. Turning off parallel query or parallel_leader_participation hides or changes the symptom but does not fix it, so the already-exists angle has nothing to raise.

This is a wrong-results bugfix, so demand is not in question. The reproduction uses default settings and plain LATERAL with a parameterized LIMIT, and a committer confirmed it in message #1. Every user who hits this plan shape gets silently wrong answers. The fix costs nothing for users who do not hit it. Back-branch ABI handling is a design question for another angle.
